mainTopic: The six נדבה collection boxes, leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה, and replacing a blemished עולה
overview: The גמרא finishes listing בר פדא's explanation of the six נדבה collection boxes (שופרות). It then explains why the other views reject each earlier explanation: חזקיה (no fear of fights), רבי יוחנן (no fear of rotting coins), זעירי (we do not set a משנה like a lone opinion), and בר פדא (his categories are all leftover money, and the מעה goes to the שקלים). Two new explanations follow. שמואל says the six boxes are for leftover money from six kinds of קרבנות, and רבי אושעיא says almost the same but puts קינין in place of the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה. The גמרא explains each one's choice, which leads to an argument over whether leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה goes to נדבה or must rot. רב חסדא and רבה read a ברייתא differently on this, matching an argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. A challenge from a משנה is answered, and רב נחמן בר רב יצחק proves from רבי יהודה's teaching that the money rots. Finally, a new משנה teaches that the redemption money of a blemished עולה may buy a different number or kind of animal, while רבי forbids this.

steps.title: Finishing the list of donation categories
steps.stepSummary: The last explanation finishes its list of six categories of funds: lambs, goats, leftover money, and the extra מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one horn was for the lambs, one for the goats, one for leftover money, and one for the extra silver מעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a list it already started before this section. Each of the six horns matched a different kind of money for offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view does not explain the six horns by priestly families or by worry about the coins. Instead, each horn matches a separate category of funds. That lets the גמרא next compare this view with the earlier explanations.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs, here meaning money set aside for lamb offerings
Goats, here meaning money for goat offerings
Leftover money, the extra that remained after buying an offering
A small silver coin, here the extra premium paid when two people gave a shekel together

phrases.english: And the lambs, and the goats,
and the leftover money, and the extra ma'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the final explanation begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the six horns was for a different category of funds: lambs, goats, leftover money, the extra מעה, plus the categories listed before.

steps.title: Why the others reject חזקיה: no worry about fights
steps.stepSummary: The other views do not accept חזקיה's reason, because there is no real chance of a fight between priestly families.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the others do not hold like חזקיה, because we are not worried about fights, since each family serves on its own day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why the other sages did not use חזקיה's explanation. It answers that his worry about fighting is not realistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה said the six horns were there to stop the priestly families from quarreling. The others answer that there is nothing to fight over. Each family works on its own fixed day, so it is clear what belongs to whom.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them, here meaning all the other sages
To quarrel or fight
We are not worried about it
He serves on his own day

phrases.english: All of them do not say like Ḥizkiyya,
we are not concerned about quarreling,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל חַד וְחַד יוֹמֵיהּ קָא עָבֵיד.
phrases.english: since each and every one serves on his own day.
phrases.notes: "Each one" means each priestly family; each has its own day of service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the views are listed, the גמרא begins explaining why each view rejects the others, starting with חזקיה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects חזקיה's reason for the six horns.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fear of quarreling is not realistic, because each family has its own fixed day.

steps.title: Why the others reject רבי יוחנן: no worry about rotting
steps.stepSummary: The other views do not accept רבי יוחנן's reason, because they are not worried that the coins will rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not hold like רבי יוחנן, because we are not worried that the money will rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same pattern. It now explains why the others reject רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said there were many horns so that coins would not pile up and rot. The others simply do not see this as a real concern. So his reason is not enough to explain six horns.

keyTerms.meaning: To rot or decay, from becoming moldy

phrases.english: They do not say like Rabbi Yoḥanan,
we are not concerned about decaying.
phrases.notes: He means the coins; the others are not afraid that stored money will go bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as the previous step, now applied to רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוחנן's reason for the six horns.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fear that the coins will rot is not considered realistic.

steps.title: Why the others reject זעירי: a משנה is not set to follow one sage alone
steps.stepSummary: The other views do not accept זעירי's approach, because we do not explain a משנה as following a lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not hold like זעירי, because we do not explain a משנה as following a single sage's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the pattern by explaining why the others reject זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי explained the משנה as following רבי, who holds a minority view. The others prefer an explanation that fits the majority. When there is another option, we do not explain a משנה as following one sage against everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A lone individual, meaning one sage's minority opinion
They do not set it up, meaning they do not explain the משנה that way

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general rule for reading a משנה: when possible, explain it so it fits the majority view and not a lone sage.

phrases.english: They do not say like Ze'eiri,
we do not establish it like a lone individual.
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה; זעירי had said it follows רבי, who is in the minority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three rejections, now applied to זעירי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects זעירי's way of explaining the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It sets the משנה as following a single minority opinion, which we avoid when another explanation is available.

steps.title: The other views reject בר פדא: all his categories are really leftover money
steps.stepSummary: The other views do not accept בר פדא's list, because the lost-animal money he counts separately is itself just leftover money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other views also do not explain it like בר פדא. Why not? He makes 'leftover money' its own category, but all the other categories are also leftover money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns down בר פדא's explanation of the six boxes, just as it turned down the earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא listed the value of lost animals as separate categories, next to a category called 'leftover money.' The other views say this split makes no sense. Once a replacement animal was brought, the money for the lost one is also just leftover money, so it all belongs in one category.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover money, the extra funds that remain after the קרבן was bought
All of them

phrases.english: They also do not say like בר פדא.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the other views, which have already turned down the earlier explanations in steps 2 through 4.

phrases.english: Leftover money? All of them are also leftover money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of rejections (steps 2 through 4), now aimed at the last explanation (בר פדא).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The separate categories in בר פדא's list
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His categories overlap: the lost-animal money is already included in 'leftover money.'

steps.title: The extra מעה does not need its own box
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection of בר פדא: the extra מעה simply goes along with the regular שקלים, so it does not get a separate box.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מעה also goes to the שקלים, so it does not need a box of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason to reject בר פדא, this time about his sixth category, the extra מעה. The next step will bring a source to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא gave the extra מעה its own box. The other views say the מעה is treated like the half-שקל itself and goes to the same place. If so, there is no reason for a separate box.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin, paid as an extra fee on top of the half-שקל
The yearly half-שקל coins that pay for the communal קרבנות

phrases.english: The מעה also
goes to the שקלים,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate reason for rejecting בר פדא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The sixth category in בר פדא's list (the מעה)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מעה goes into the general שקלים fund, so it does not need its own box.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows where the extra fee goes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records an argument: רבי מאיר says the extra fee goes to the שקלים, and רבי אליעזר says it goes to communal נדבה offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Where does this extra fee go? To the שקלים, says רבי מאיר. רבי אליעזר says: to communal gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what it just said, that the מעה goes to the שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says it outright: the קלבון goes to the שקלים, together with the regular half-שקל money. The other views follow רבי מאיר, so the מעה needs no separate box. רבי אליעזר disagrees and sends it to נדבה offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra fee paid on top of the half-שקל (the same thing as the מעה)
A voluntary gift offering; here, communal offerings bought with spare funds

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Where does this extra fee go?
To the שקלים. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי אליעזר says: to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind step 6's claim.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the מעה goes to the שקלים and does not get its own box
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא containing the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אליעזר
steps.whatToRemember: Every earlier explanation of the six boxes is rejected. חזקיה is rejected because there is no fear of fighting, רבי יוחנן because there is no fear of rotting, and זעירי because we do not explain a משנה as a lone opinion. בר פדא is rejected because his categories are all leftover money, and because the מעה goes to the שקלים.

steps.title: שמואל: six boxes for money left over from six kinds of קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the six boxes are for money left over from a חטאת, an אשם, the אשם of a נזיר, the אשם of a מצורע, a מנחת חוטא, and the עשירית האיפה of the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: the six boxes match up with leftover money from six offerings: a חטאת, an אשם, a נזיר's אשם, a מצורע's אשם, a sinner's מנחה, and the כהן גדול's tenth-of-an-איפה offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a brand-new explanation of the six boxes, in the name of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of mixing animal values with other funds, שמואל sorts the boxes by which קרבן the money came from. Each box holds the money left over after buying one specific kind of offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Matching up with, one for each
Money left over after buying a חטאת
The אשם a נזיר brings, for example after becoming טמא from a dead body
The אשם a מצורע brings as part of becoming טהור
The flour offering a poor sinner brings in place of a חטאת
The daily flour offering of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: And שמואל says: they match the leftover money of a sin offering,
and the leftover money of a guilt offering, and the leftover money of a nazirite's guilt offering,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹתַר אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע, וּמוֹתַר מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא,
phrases.english: and the leftover money of a leper's guilt offering, and the leftover money of a sinner's meal offering,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹתַר עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: and the leftover money of the High Priest's tenth of an ephah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier explanations were rejected, the גמרא offers a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six boxes hold money left over from six specific kinds of קרבנות, with the עשירית האיפה of the כהן גדול as the sixth.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: almost the same list, but with bird pairs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא gives a list like שמואל's, but he counts leftover money from קינין (bird pairs) instead of the כהן גדול's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא says: the six boxes match up with leftover money from a חטאת, an אשם, a נזיר's אשם, a מצורע's אשם, bird pairs, and a sinner's מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more explanation of the six boxes, from רבי אושעיא, which differs from שמואל's in one item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five of the six items are the same as שמואל's. The difference is the sixth. רבי אושעיא leaves out the עשירית האיפה of the כהן גדול and puts in leftover money from קינין.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of birds (doves or pigeons), brought for example by a woman after birth or by a זב

steps.whatToRemember: There are two new explanations of the six boxes. שמואל and רבי אושעיא agree on five kinds of leftover קרבן money. They differ only on the sixth: שמואל says the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה, and רבי אושעיא says קינין.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד מוֹתַר חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: And רבי אושעיא says: they match the leftover money of a sin offering,
and the leftover money of a guilt offering, and the leftover money of a nazirite's guilt offering,
and the leftover money of a leper's guilt offering, and the leftover money of bird pairs,
and the leftover money of a sinner's meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד מוֹתַר חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second new explanation, set side by side with שמואל's, differing only in one item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six boxes hold money left over from six kinds of קרבנות, with קינין in place of the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה.

steps.title: Why does שמואל not count קינין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל does not list leftover קינין money the way רבי אושעיא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל, what is his reason that he does not say like רבי אושעיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the two lists from Steps 8 and 9. It asks why שמואל does not count קינין like רבי אושעיא, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists have six items and share five of them. The only difference is the sixth item, so the גמרא asks each אמורא to explain his choice. It starts with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Pairs of birds brought as offerings

phrases.english: And שמואל, what is the reason
that he does not say like רבי אושעיא?
phrases.notes: He means: why doesn't שמואל count leftover קינין money as one of the six boxes?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two lists given in Steps 8 and 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why שמואל leaves קינין out of the six boxes

steps.title: קינין are already listed earlier in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל leaves out קינין because the משנה already lists a קינין box in its first part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה already taught קינין in its first part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה in שקלים already names a box for קינין among the earlier boxes. So שמואל does not count it again among the six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists several boxes for specific uses before it gets to the six נדבה boxes. A box for קינין is already in that earlier list. Counting it again would mean the משנה repeats itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Pairs of birds, it already taught in the first part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קינין already have their own box in the רישא, so they cannot be one of the six

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's version also lists קינין earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אושעיא's version of the משנה also lists קינין earlier, so how can he count it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי אושעיא teach the משנה without listing קינין? But רבי אושעיא does teach it, and he lists קינין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. רבי אושעיא's version of the משנה also has the קינין box in the first part, so the same problem should apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the answer in Step 11 is right, רבי אושעיא would be counting קינין twice. Unless his משנה leaves out the earlier קינין box, his list seems to repeat an item. The גמרא says his משנה does include it.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't he teach? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא תָּנֵי, וְלָא תָּנֵי קִינִּין?
phrases.english: And does רבי אושעיא teach it and not teach pairs of birds?
phrases.notes: He means: does רבי אושעיא's version of the משנה leave out the earlier קינין box?

phrases.english: But רבי אושעיא does teach it, and he teaches pairs of birds!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא תָּנֵי, וְלָא תָּנֵי קִינִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of Step 11 into a problem for רבי אושעיא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's counting of קינין among the six boxes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own משנה already has a קינין box earlier, so counting קינין again would be a repeat

steps.title: One box for קינין, one for leftover קינין money
steps.stepSummary: There are two separate boxes: one for buying קינין and one for money left over from קינין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One box is for קינין, and one box is for leftover קינין money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two boxes are not the same. The earlier box holds money for buying קינין, and רבי אושעיא's box holds money left over after buying them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the two boxes are told apart, רבי אושעיא is not repeating anything. The leftover money goes to a נדבה box, which is a different use from the money set aside to buy birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Money left over after buying the pairs of birds
One

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two boxes. The earlier box is for buying birds. The box among the six is only for leftover money from קינין.

phrases.english: One is for pairs of birds, and one is for leftover money from pairs of birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both boxes are the same קינין box, so רבי אושעיא repeats an item
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier box is for buying קינין, and his box is for leftover קינין money

steps.title: Why does רבי אושעיא not count the כהן גדול's offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אושעיא does not list the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה the way שמואל does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אושעיא, what is his reason that he does not say like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the opposite question. Why does רבי אושעיא leave out the כהן גדול's offering, which שמואל counts? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know why שמואל does not count קינין. The other half of the difference still needs an explanation: why רבי אושעיא leaves out the leftover money of the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth of an איפה, the daily flour offering of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: And רבי אושעיא, what is the reason
that he does not say like שמואל?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of the question in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אושעיא leaves the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה out of the six boxes

steps.title: Leftover money from the כהן גדול's offering must rot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא holds that leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה is left to rot, so it never goes to a נדבה box.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the opinion that says leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה is left to rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אושעיא follows the opinion that this leftover money is not used at all. It is left to rot, so there is no נדבה box for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The six boxes are only for leftover money that goes to communal נדבה. If this money may not be used, it cannot have one of those boxes. That leaves room for קינין in רבי אושעיא's list.

keyTerms.meaning: It must rot, meaning it is left unused until it is ruined
Like the one who says (following a certain opinion)
The High Priest

phrases.english: He holds like the one who says:
The leftover money of the tenth of an איפה
of the כהן גדול must be left to rot,
phrases.notes: "Rot" here means the money may not be used, so it is put away until it is lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He holds that leftover money from the כהן גדול's offering must rot, so it never goes to נדבה
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the two lists are not just different counts. They come from a real argument about what happens to leftover money from the כהן גדול's offering.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows this opinion exists
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one kind of leftover מנחה money goes to נדבה and another kind must rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: leftover money of a מנחת goes to נדבה; leftover money of a מנחה must rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that someone really does hold that some leftover מנחה money must rot. The wording is unclear, and the next step asks about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up two kinds of מנחה with two different outcomes. One goes to נדבה and one is left to rot. As written, though, it does not say which מנחה is which.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary communal offering bought with the money
Leftover money

phrases.english: As it is taught: the leftover of the meal offering of — goes to a gift offering,
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off after "meal offering of" without saying whose; the next steps fill this in.

phrases.english: the leftover of a meal offering — must rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the opinion mentioned in Step 15
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that leftover money from the כהן גדול's offering must rot
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that separates leftover money that goes to נדבה from leftover money that must rot

steps.title: What does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unclear wording of the ברייתא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the ברייתא is saying, since the wording does not make clear which מנחה it means. This sets up רב חסדא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As written, the ברייתא seems to give two opposite rulings for the same "מנחה." The גמרא needs to know which two מנחות it is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (asking to explain unclear wording)

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear wording of the ברייתא in Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מנחה goes to נדבה and which must rot

steps.title: רב חסדא explains: מנחת חוטא goes to נדבה, the כהן גדול's offering rots
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that leftover מנחת חוטא money goes to נדבה, and leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה must rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this is what it means. Leftover money of a מנחת חוטא goes to נדבה. Leftover money of the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה must rot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא fills in the missing words of the ברייתא. The first case is the מנחת חוטא, and the second is the כהן גדול's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once it is read this way, the ברייתא clearly says that leftover money from the כהן גדול's offering must rot. That is exactly the view רבי אושעיא follows. So he leaves it off his list, while both he and שמואל keep מנחת חוטא as a נדבה box.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering of a sinner who is too poor to bring an animal or birds
This is what it means

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל counts the כהן גדול's offering and not קינין, because a קינין box is already listed earlier. רבי אושעיא counts leftover קינין money, which is a different box, and not the כהן גדול's offering, because he holds that leftover money from it must rot.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said: this is what it is saying —
the leftover of a sinner's meal offering goes to a gift offering,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹתַר עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל – יִרְקַב.
phrases.english: the leftover of the tenth of an איפה of the כהן גדול — must rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 and finishes the proof for Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first case is a מנחת חוטא, which goes to נדבה; the second is the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה, which must rot

steps.title: רבה's different reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה says leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה also goes to נדבה. The leftover money that must rot is from לחמי תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Even leftover money from the כהן גדול's tenth-of-an-איפה offering goes to נדבה. The leftover money that must rot is money left from buying the loaves of a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה offers a second way to explain the same unclear ברייתא that רב חסדא just explained. He disagrees with רב חסדא about which leftover money must rot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the money that rots is the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה money. רבה moves that money into the נדבה group. He says the case that rots is leftover money from לחמי תודה instead. Both agree that one case goes to נדבה and one rots. They only disagree about which case is which.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves of bread brought together with a קרבן תודה (thanksgiving offering)
It must rot: the money is put away and left unused until it is lost
Here, a communal gift offering bought with leftover money
Also, too

steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רב חסדא read the same unclear ברייתא in two different ways. Both agree that one case goes to נדבה and one case rots. They argue only about which case belongs on which side.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Even the leftover money of the tenth of an ephah
of the High Priest also goes to a gift offering,
rather, the leftover money of the thanks-offering loaves must rot.
phrases.notes: He is saying which case in the ברייתא is the one that rots. In his reading it is the תודה loaves, not the כהן גדול's offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מוֹתַר עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the ברייתא that disagrees with רב חסדא's explanation in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the unclear ברייתא mean? (from step 17)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן גדול's leftover עשירית האיפה money goes to נדבה. The leftover money from לחמי תודה must rot.

steps.title: The same question is argued by רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the question is an older argument: רבי יוחנן says the leftover money goes to נדבה, and רבי אלעזר says it must rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the subject of an argument. About leftover money from the כהן גדול's tenth-of-an-איפה offering, רבי יוחנן says it goes to נדבה, and רבי אלעזר says it must rot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument between רב חסדא and רבה matches an argument between earlier אמוראים. This also sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's view (נדבה) matches רבה. רבי אלעזר's view (rot) matches רב חסדא. The גמרא now has a clear position to test, and the next step challenges רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the subject of an argument, meaning the same question was already argued by earlier sages

phrases.english: It is the subject of a dispute:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹתַר עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: the leftover money of the High Priest's tenth of an ephah,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it goes to a gift offering,
Rabbi Elazar says: it must rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the two explanations from steps 18 and 19 to an earlier argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה goes to נדבה. רבי אלעזר: it must rot.

steps.title: A משנה lists leftover עשירית האיפה money as going to נדבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר with a משנה. The משנה says leftover עשירית האיפה money, like the leftover money of several other offerings, goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Leftover שקלים money is חולין. But leftover money of the tenth of an איפה, and leftover money of the bird-pairs of זבים, זבות and women after childbirth, and of חטאות and אשמות, all go to נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to challenge רבי אלעזר. This step only quotes the source, and the next step will show how it hurts רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה places leftover עשירית האיפה money in the נדבה group, together with leftover money for other required offerings. רבי אלעזר said the כהן גדול's leftover money must rot. So if this משנה is talking about the כהן גדול, it contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover money set aside to pay the yearly half-שקל
Not holy: ordinary money that can be used for anything
The pairs of birds brought by a man or woman who became טמא from a flow
Women who gave birth, who bring a pair of birds
Sin offerings and guilt offerings

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
leftover shekel money is non-sacred,
and the leftover money of the tenth of an ephah,
and the leftover money of the bird-pairs of zavim and the bird-pairs of zavot
and the bird-pairs of women after childbirth, and sin offerings and guilt offerings,
their leftover money goes to a gift offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to challenge רבי אלעזר's view from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר, who says leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה must rot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says leftover עשירית האיפה money goes to נדבה. That seems to go against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: Isn't the משנה talking about the כהן גדול's offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes the challenge sharp: the עשירית האיפה in the משנה seems to be the כהן גדול's, which goes against רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't "leftover money of the tenth of an איפה" mean the כהן גדול's tenth of an איפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה is a problem for רבי אלעזר. It suggests that the unnamed עשירית האיפה in the משנה is the כהן גדול's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "מאי לאו" ("isn't it...?") offer the most natural reading of the משנה. On that reading, the משנה says the כהן גדול's leftover money goes to נדבה, which is the opposite of what רבי אלעזר said. A defense of רבי אלעזר will have to read the משנה another way.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it...?": a way of suggesting how to read a source so that it challenges someone

steps.confusionAlert: This is still a suggestion, not a final ruling. "מאי לאו" often leads to an answer that reads the source differently.

phrases.english: Is it not that
the leftover money of the tenth of an ephah
is that of the High Priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from step 21 by saying the משנה refers to the כהן גדול's offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that the כהן גדול's leftover money must rot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה's unnamed עשירית האיפה is the כהן גדול's, then the משנה clearly says its leftover money goes to נדבה, against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The משנה means the sinner's meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר: the עשירית האיפה in the משנה is the מנחת חוטא, not the כהן גדול's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is talking about leftover money from the meal offering of a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רבי אלעזר. It says the משנה's 'עשירית האיפה' is really the poor sinner's meal offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת חוטא is also a tenth of an איפה of flour, so the משנה's words can fit it. That means the משנה never said anything about the כהן גדול's offering, and רבי אלעזר is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering a very poor person brings for certain sins instead of an animal or birds
Leftover money set aside for an offering but not needed

steps.confusionAlert: Two different offerings are called 'a tenth of an איפה': the כהן גדול's daily one and the poor sinner's one. The whole answer depends on telling them apart.

phrases.english: No, it means the leftover money of a sinner's meal offering.
phrases.notes: The 'tenth of an איפה' in the משנה is the poor sinner's offering (ויקרא 5:11), not the כהן גדול's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 21–22 against רבי אלעזר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting which case the משנה is talking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's עשירית האיפה is the כהן גדול's offering, which goes against רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's עשירית האיפה is the מנחת חוטא, so it says nothing against רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר רב יצחק favors the view that the money rots
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב יצחק says it is more logical that leftover money from the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה must rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב יצחק said: It makes sense to follow the one who said the leftover money of the כהן גדול's tenth of an איפה must rot.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא takes a side in the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. He is setting up a proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא only defended רבי אלעזר from a challenge. Now רב נחמן בר רב יצחק goes further and says רבי אלעזר's view (it rots) is actually the more logical one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable / it makes sense
The כהן גדול's daily meal offering of a tenth of an איפה of flour
Let it rot. The money is left unused until it is lost.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Yitzchak said:
It is reasonable to follow the one who said:
phrases.notes: 'The one who said' is רבי אלעזר from step 20.

phrases.aramaic: מוֹתַר עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל יִרְקַב.
phrases.english: The leftover money of the High Priest's tenth of an ephah must rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי אלעזר, the גמרא now brings an opinion that supports him
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is more logical that the leftover money of the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה must rot.

steps.title: Only the sinner's meal offering is called a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה learns from the פסוק that only the מנחת חוטא is called a חטאת. So the כהן גדול's offering is not called a חטאת, and it needs לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'He shall put no oil on it, nor put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.' רבי יהודה said: This one is called a 'sin offering,' and no other one is called a 'sin offering.' This teaches that the כהן גדול's tenth of an איפה is not called a 'sin offering,' and it needs frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר רב יצחק brings a ברייתא as the source for his view. It shows the כהן גדול's offering is not in the 'חטאת' group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it is a sin offering' are read as narrowing: only the מנחת חוטא gets that name. The כהן גדול's offering is left out, so it does not get the חטאת rules and does need לבונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense put on most meal offerings
Sin offering
Is called (has the name of)
It taught (a lesson learned from the פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'He shall put no oil upon it,'
nor shall he put frankincense upon it,
for it is a sin offering.'
Rabbi Yehuda said: It is called a 'sin offering,'
phrases.notes: He is reading the word 'הִיא' ('it') as 'only it.'

phrases.english: and no other meal offering is called a 'sin offering.'

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: This taught about the High Priest's tenth of an ephah
that it is not called a 'sin offering,'
and so it needs frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רב נחמן בר רב יצחק's view
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר רב יצחק's view that the money rots
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה reads 'כי חטאת היא' as meaning only the מנחת חוטא is called a חטאת

steps.title: Not called a חטאת, so its leftover money rots
steps.stepSummary: Since the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה is not called a חטאת, its leftover money does not go to נדבה. It must rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since it is not called a 'sin offering,' its leftover money must rot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר רב יצחק finishes his proof. He draws the money rule from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא itself only spoke about לבונה. רב נחמן בר רב יצחק takes one more step: an offering that is not called a חטאת does not get the חטאת rule for leftover money. So he sides with רבי אלעזר that the money rots.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is not
Its leftover money

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר is defended: the משנה is about the מנחת חוטא. רב נחמן בר רב יצחק backs him with רבי יהודה's teaching. The כהן גדול's offering is not called a חטאת, so its leftover money rots.

phrases.english: And since it is not called a 'sin offering,'
its leftover money must rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical money rule out of the ברייתא in step 25
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה is not called a חטאת, so its leftover money must rot, like רבי אלעזר says.

steps.title: A blemished bull's money: one bull can become two, and two can become one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a bull promised as an עולה gets a blemish, he may buy two bulls with its money. If two bulls get blemishes, he may buy one bull with their money. רבי forbids this.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone said, "This bull is an עולה," and it got a blemish, he may, if he wants, bring two bulls with its money. If he said, "These two bulls are an עולה," and they got blemishes, he may, if he wants, bring one bull with their money. And רבי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches that the redemption money of a blemished עולה bull does not have to buy exactly the same number of bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot go on the מזבח, so it is redeemed and the money buys a replacement. The תנא קמא allows one bull's money to buy two cheaper bulls, and two bulls' money to buy one bigger bull. רבי disagrees and forbids at least the second case, so two bulls must stay two bulls.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
It got a blemish and can no longer be brought as a קרבן
Its money: the redemption money of the blemished animal
Forbids

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the blemished bull itself is brought. It cannot go on the מזבח at all. Only the money it is redeemed for is used to buy new animals.

phrases.english: MISHNA
If one said, "This bull is a burnt offering," and it became blemished,
if he wishes, he may bring two with its money.
If one said, "These two bulls are a burnt offering," and they became blemished,
if he wishes, he may bring one with their money,
and Rabbi forbids it.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא. He says the two bulls must be replaced by two bulls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the conclusion about the כהן גדול's עשירית האיפה in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption money of a blemished עולה bull may buy two bulls instead of one, or one bull instead of two. רבי forbids this.

steps.title: A blemished ram's money can buy a lamb, and a lamb's money can buy a ram
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if a ram promised as an עולה gets a blemish, he may buy a lamb with its money. If a lamb gets a blemish, he may buy a ram with its money. רבי forbids this.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said, "This ram is an עולה," and it got a blemish, he may, if he wants, bring a lamb with its money. If he said, "This lamb is an עולה," and it got a blemish, he may, if he wants, bring a ram with its money. And רבי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from changing the number of animals to changing the kind of animal. The תנא קמא allows switching between a ram and a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ram is an older, bigger sheep and a lamb is a young one. The תנא קמא allows the money to go either way, so a ram can be replaced by a cheaper lamb and a lamb by a more expensive ram. רבי forbids buying a different kind of animal with the redemption money.

keyTerms.meaning: A ram, a grown male sheep
A lamb, a young sheep
If he wishes. It is allowed but not required.

steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה the תנא קמא lets the redemption money of a blemished עולה change both the number of animals and the kind of animal. רבי forbids these changes.

phrases.english: If one said, "This ram is a burnt offering," and it became blemished,
if he wishes, he may bring a lamb with its money.
If one said, "This lamb is a burnt offering," and it became blemished,
if he wishes, he may bring a ram with its money,
and Rabbi forbids it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Could be read as part of one combined משנה step with step 27.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from a change in number (step 27) to a change in kind of animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption money of a blemished עולה ram may buy a lamb, and a blemished lamb's money may buy a ram. רבי forbids this.
